title: CDC and NIOSH Staffing Cuts Prompt Concern About Public-Health Capacity
description_short: CDC and NIOSH Staffing Cuts Prompt Concern About Public-Health Capacity
description_medium: AFGE says HHS continued public health layoffs despite reinstatements and describes cuts at CDC and NIOSH as threats to frontline science and programs. The linked article also refers to a May 14 union lawsuit seeking reversal of NIOSH layoffs. It documents the union’s account of ongoing reductions, not that all outbreak-response capacity was eliminated or every targeted employee was separated.
description_long: Federal health agencies underwent layoffs early in 2025 as bird flu continued to spread and a measles outbreak grew in the Southwest. NPR reported that recent CDC firings primarily targeted new and temporary workers. More than half a dozen current staff, speaking anonymously, worried the cuts and policy changes could weaken outbreak response; their concern was not evidence that the CDC had lost its ability to respond. Later, the American Federation of Government Employees said more than 1,500 CDC employees and over 90% of NIOSH staff had been targeted, and that about 300 NIOSH workers were reinstated. AFGE described continued layoffs and referred to a May 14 union lawsuit seeking reversal of NIOSH cuts. The sources distinguish targeted employees from people whose separations were completed. They document staff concerns and union claims about staffing reductions, not an elimination of disease surveillance, FEMA capacity, or emergency response programs, nor a measured increase in illness or deaths.

title: Reviews Find DOGE Savings Claims Exceeded Verifiable Amounts in Separate Samples
description_short: CBS and Politico reviews found DOGE savings claims far above verifiable amounts in distinct analyses.
description_medium: CBS News reviewed three large HHS contract cancellations that DOGE listed as $6.4 billion in savings and estimated the actual savings at about $165 million. A separate Politico review found that DOGE’s $52.8 billion contract-savings claim through July was far above what could be verified from public records. These analyses used different sets and methods; neither means every DOGE savings claim was false or establishes the full amount ultimately saved.
description_long: Two reviews in the supplied account compare DOGE’s reported contract savings with amounts the reviewers could verify, but they examine different sets and use different methods. CBS News reviewed three large HHS contract cancellations that DOGE listed as $6.4 billion in savings and estimated the actual savings at about $165 million. That estimate applies to those three HHS cancellations; it is not a result for all DOGE activity. Separately, a Politico review found that DOGE’s $52.8 billion contract-savings claim through July was far above what could be verified from public records. The supplied material does not give a precise Politico verified total in the clean medium. These are two distinct comparisons, so their figures should not be combined into one rate or treated as results from the same sample. Neither analysis means every DOGE savings claim was false, and neither establishes the full amount ultimately saved. This entry describes the reported gap between the claims and the amounts the reviews could verify, with those limits kept explicit.
